utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. No preliminaries, therefore the witness can be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Andan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, I'd like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Ms. Bibles will now continue her cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Andan. When we finished --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: When we finished on Friday, you answered questions about events leading up to the operation against the Yellow Wasps. Before we go back to that line of inquiry, I'd like to ask about some of the paramilitary -- other paramilitary formations which were undermining the war effort for which you had personal knowledge. Was one of these paramilitary groups that you dealt with the Panthers led by Mauzer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, in fact, at one point during the summer of 1992, isn't it true that you arrested or detained Mauzer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In legal terms, it would be better to say that I brought him into custody and that he was remanded.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Is it true that his side-arm, a Heckler with a silencer, was removed at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And would you agree that the underlying facts which led to this bringing him into custody had to do with a large amount of stolen property and the illegal detention of three Muslim men?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That first time when he was brought into custody, it did not have to do directly with what you referred to just now. That first part had to do with constant attacks and denying the Ministry of the Interior -- or, rather, not carrying out legal regulations in the municipality of Bijeljina. That's why he was brought in for the first time. Whereas the second time, it was based on the intelligence that we had; namely, that certain illegally obtained goods were being stored and that that warehouse should be entered, that we should check what is there, and at that point in time we did not know that in part of this cooling plant that hadn't been used at the time, that detained Muslims were actually being held there in part of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And addressing your attention to this second time, can you describe whether it's true that the Panthers surrounded the police station with tanks and weapons?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. Surrounded us because they were dissatisfied with the fact that their supporters were being brought in; that is to say, their fighters who were bringing looted goods in from the front line. They surrounded us using all kinds of weapons, asking that we - that is to say, Mr. Davidovic and I - should no longer be at the helm of the security services centre in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Do you recall roughly when this occurred?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the month of July, before the operation in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Can you confirm that once the police station was surrounded, you were in that situation, that an agreement was reached in which Mauzer was released but his side-arm was not given back to him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Is it your opinion, based on your experience and dealings with Mauzer, that he is a criminal?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, I as a policeman ran a check on Mauzer. I did not find him registered in police records. He did not have a criminal record. But all the other manifestations that were there, all of the things that happened during the war lead me to ascertain the fact that he took advantage of the war in order to engage in criminal activity.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Is it true that Mauzer was never prosecuted for offences that he and his men committed in 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the premises were searched, the ones that you referred to a moment ago, where we found the detained Muslims, a criminal report was filed. I claim that with certainty. And it was sent to the prosecutor's office. Now, why it was not dealt with any further than that, I really cannot tell you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Just to make sure that we have a clear answer to the question, you would agree or is it true that he was never prosecuted for those offences?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was not tried as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: In terms of the stolen property that was recovered, your answer as to what happened to that property was addressed in the Stanisic/Zupljanin trial at transcript page 21444, lines 23 and 24. And your answer was: "Mauzer's unit should have been resubordinated to the VRS according to the command structure and we gave these items to the army." Do you stand by that answer today?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All the time we tried not to have Mauzer's paramilitary unit in Bijeljina. We talked to Colonel Milic several times to have him placed under control. Therefore, we called the members of the military after we found what we found at the warehouse and the military police took over everything that was found at that warehouse. It wasn't really a warehouse, it was a cooling plant but they used it as a warehouse. So it was handed over to the military police and an inventory was made.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: In terms of Mauzer's role with the VRS, let's go to 65 ter 1925, a commendation of the VRS dated 9 March 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we can go -- I believe it's just a one-page -- or to the first page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: When the document comes up - yes, it's probably a good time to put on your glasses - I'll ask if you know what type of document this is. Mr. Andan, having been in the VRS for a number of years, are you familiar with this type of document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with this type of document.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And what is it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you allow me, I'm going to make a brief introduction. I will try to be as brief as possible. In that year, in 1992, towards the end, as far as I know, perhaps it was September or October, Mauzer was included in the Army of Republika Srpska in the Eastern Bosnian Corps; that is to say, from then onwards, it is the VRS that had control over Mauzer. This document speaks about his combat activities at a given point in time. I mean, he --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Andan --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- demonstrated bravery and decisiveness and --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: -- we're getting ahead of ourselves, and I guess I should ask it a different way: You will agree that this document is a commendation being given by Mr. Mladic or General Mladic at the time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: You see in the document that the Mauzer combat group was being commended specifically for toughness, chivalrous and gallant conduct. Now, Mr. Andan, that does not comport with the description of the Mauzer group that you dealt with in 1992. Does it bother you at all that a criminal like Mauzer received such high praise?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, shall we make a distinction between a person and a group to start with? And second, if you just want to jump from 1992 to 1995 in a totally different area, perhaps don't stop the witness if he makes the bridge which you should have made. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, you have given a description of what happened with Mauzer or Mauzer's group as they went on, and my question was: Even acknowledging that, that there were different activities, knowing what you know about Mauzer and the Panthers in 1992, did it bother you that he went on to receive this kind of praise in the war?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I view this as a commendation to the unit. I agree with you that he did not deserve this kind of commendation, but the unit as a unit did deserve a commendation.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender 65 ter 1925.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1925 receives number P6579, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have one question for you, sir. This group that surrounded the police station with a tank, is it the same group of Mauzer's that was being commended in 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Next I'd like to turn and ask about your information and contacts with members of Arkan's Men. Is it correct that in Bijeljina, in 1992, Arkan's Men unlawfully took a large quantity of weapons from the police station that had been confiscated from the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only weapons, that's true, they took all those weapons, everything that suited them, they took that. They took a large number of traffic documents, driver's licenses, stamps, and other documents that were blank. So they took all of this that can be found in any legal department, if you will.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Based upon your work in 1992, do you think that there was a link between Arkan's Men and Mauzer's Panthers at that time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think. I cannot say with certainty now. I don't think that it was a link then, because I know once when Arkan visited Bijeljina that some colleagues said to me that he had some kind of conflict with Mauzer and that he threatened him at that point, but all of this is indirect knowledge. It's not that I know it personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, obviously we've discussed your testimony in Stanisic/Zupljanin. Do you recall answering similar questions during that trial?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And the transcript references would be 21653, starting at line 4. You were asked the question: "And what was the relationship, if any, that you know about between Mauzer's group and Arkan's Men? Were they in competition with each other, were they co-operating with each other? What do you know about that?" Your answer was: "I'll begin with a short introduction, so I hope you won't mind a longer answer. "At that time the Bijeljina police station was exposed to strong influence by Arkan's group. Through operative work, we learned that they had unlawfully taken a large quantity of weapons, both long-barrelled and short-barrelled weapons, that had been confiscated from the Muslims. They were registering these weapons at the Bijeljina police station without anyone interfering. They were taking driving licences, traffic permits, weapons permits from the police station, even blank forms for such licences and permits. "I think that there was a link between the Serb Volunteer Guard commanded by Arkan, and the Panthers commanded by Ljubisa Savic, also known as Mauzer. It was my conclusion that I drew from various conversations and interviews that they were in direct communication." Can you tell us whether your opinion about this connection or link has changed since your testimony in Stanisic and Zupljanin?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it hasn't changed, but I know for sure that when the war conflict broke out, there was this "love" and it went on probably until a moment when a conflict broke out for this or that reason. But at any rate, at the moment when I arrived in Bijeljina, that was July, that love was not the same as it was in the beginning of the war. So there is no change in my statement today as compared to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Perhaps we could clear up this confusion. Is it your answer today that there was a link between these two groups, Arkan's Men and Mauzer's Panthers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I'd next like to address how groups like Arkan's Men and Mauzer's Panthers originally came to Bosnia. Are you aware that members of the Bosnian Serb leadership invited groups like this into Bosnia at the beginning of the war?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was still in Sarajevo then when Arkan entered Bijeljina together with his unit. When three members of the Presidency, Biljana Plavsic, Fikret Abdic - now, was he a member of the Presidency, but he was on this delegation - and the minister of defence, a Croat, when they came to Bijeljina, I know that on television then, as far as I can remember, Biljana Plavsic stated that she had invited Arkan to come to Bijeljina. If I remember that period, 1992, correctly, it could have even been the month of March. So Biljana took upon herself the responsibility of having Arkan invited to Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'd next like to go to Zvornik which was where the Yellow Wasps operation took place. Were you aware of the expulsion of Muslims from Kozluk in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: When intelligence was being carried out in the field, of course we learned about that, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 19766 on our screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, this is a Drina Corps command report from 17 December 1992. I'll first ask if you have seen this report before.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't seen this before.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'd ask you to turn your attention to the bottom of the first page --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And that should be in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: -- in the paragraph that reads: "With the arrival of paramilitary organisations to the Zvornik municipality, particularly the arrival of Arkan and his people, this territory was liberated from the Turks. Turks made up 60 per cent of the municipality's population and it has now been cleansed and replaced with an ethnically pure Serb population." I first want to clarify that in this command report the word "Turks" referred to Muslims; is that true?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And second, isn't it true that the actions of the paramilitaries against Muslims and Croats was supported and commended by the VRS in the war?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know of any such cases, but the local authorities did do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, wouldn't you agree that this Drina Corps document is in fact noting in a positive manner that Zvornik was ethnically cleansed by paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it also refers to looting and taking away the property seized by paramilitary formations.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: So, Mr. Andan, isn't it true that the actions that were supported and commended by the VRS in this document were the actions where they were ethnically cleansing areas like Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We cannot generalise as far as the VRS is concerned. This is just a unit - I mean, a local unit - that is doing that. I cannot say on a general level that the army had accepted that, that the Main Staff had accepted that, and that he commended that kind of conduct. But it is evident -- I mean, now, where is this here? Which formation? This document was written, yes, and it's in the superlative, that is to say, the part that refers to that cleansing of the Muslim population.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: So, Mr. Andan, wouldn't you agree that this document sets up a scenario that you saw over and over again in Bosnia, and that is the paramilitaries were welcomed and praised for their actions in ethnically cleansing areas, but when they became problems, it was when they were looting and stealing from Serbs; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with you. From the moment when I joined the Main Staff, at regular briefings concern was expressed or, rather, there were efforts made to eliminate paramilitary formations from all of the areas. In my previous testimony here, I said that they had not been everywhere in all the territories that were under the control of the Army of Republika Srpska. Paramilitaries chose affluent places where they could loot and transfer the looted goods to Serbia and elsewhere. That's how they functioned throughout 1992, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, isn't it true that by the time you were in the VRS, which would have been September 1992, that the paramilitaries' work in those affluent regions in cleansing the area had been completed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't completed. My task, if I had not been transferred to the Army Republika Srpska under the circumstances that you are familiar with, would have been to go to Foca with the forces of the Ministry of the Interior, and we were to deal with the paramilitaries in Foca, Pelcer [phoen], and that siege should have spread across the territory of Republika Srpska. In 1992, there were a lot of places where there were paramilitary formations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, you put to the witness earlier that -- you asked him whether this was not reflecting a scenario which you would find elsewhere as well, including that the paramilitaries were welcomed, but then they became a problem when they were looting and stealing from Serbs. Now, from the portion you read to the witness, it -- I do not see that they were looting and stealing from Serbs, rather that they were perhaps looting and stealing. Could you tell us or put to the witness where you found what you said this -- what this document demonstrates? The witness hasn't seen it before, he told us, so it's only fair to him that you read to him the portions you are implicitly referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Perhaps I was jumping ahead. At line -- transcript line 10 or page 10, lines 23 and 24, the witness himself went into the looting and taking away of properties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I agree, however, it does not say regarding Serbs. So I'll clarify that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that's one. And second, the document doesn't say so. So you are --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- seeking confirmation of a -- more or less a standard scenario, where the factual description of that scenario is missing in this respect and where the document, at least what you read to him, does not say it either.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: It will be -- I'll --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'll withdraw that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- keep that in the back of your mind. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: There are a number of documents we'll be looking at, Your Honour, and I apologise for jumping the gun, so to speak, there.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Andan --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And actually, first I'd like to tender 19766.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 19766 receives number P7580, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it 75 or 65? Madam Registrar? Is it --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I apologise, it's P6580, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And admitted under that number.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: We'll return a little later to more of the details about paramilitaries, but I would like to go back now to the operation against the Yellow Wasps. On Friday you indicated that the operation started in the second half of July. Now, you've indicated some personal challenges in remembering exact dates, so let's take a look at a document that might refresh your memory.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 1D2255 on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, Mr. Andan, this appears to be a report drafted by you on the 1st of August, 1992. As this has come on our screens, have I described that document accurately?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not the right document. This is a combat report.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Who drafted this combat report?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our daily task was to inform the ministry about the situation on the front line in our area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Let's see. This is the correct document. Let's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's see. Mr. Andan, the question was whether this report was drafted by you. That's the simple question. Is it, whether it's the right or the wrong document, the one you have on your screen --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I can remember, the question and the document should both refer to the paramilitaries in Zvornik and their arrest. However, this is a report from the front line for that day. If I understood the Prosecutor properly. And I did draft this document -- or, rather, I signed it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was the question, I think. Please proceed, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, I'll --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that that was the question. It wasn't the question, but you can check. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, I'll be -- try to be very specific in my questions so that we don't have confusion. I ask you to look at the penultimate sentence in this document that reads: "The operation to mop up Zvornik is yielding positive results with regard to security and general situation in Zvornik." I have three questions. First, reading this and looking at the date, are you able now to tell us when the operation against the Yellow Wasps actually began?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, I don't have that sentence here. Do you want me to read the document to you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any confusion as to what the witness has on the screen and what we have on our screen? Do you see a document with some handwritten text at the top and at -- there is a -- the line just above where the main text starts reads: "Your dispatch number 10-11/92 of 17 July 1992." Is that the document you have before you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, now I can see it. I have that document. "The operation to mop up Zvornik is yielding positive results with regard to the security and general situation in Zvornik." Yes, this is the document. I apologise. Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please, Ms. Bibles, repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, reading this document with the date, are you now able to tell us when the operation against the Yellow Wasps would have begun?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Can you tell us that date?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Would it have been a few days before this document was drafted, or weeks, or can you give us a rough time-frame?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that it was weeks, but it was days before.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether the VRS was involved at this stage in the operation against the Yellow Wasps?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were involved.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: You were asked to comment on this particular sentence when you testified in the Stanisic/Zupljanin trial, and you said in part: "... we had practically completed this operation by wiping out these and actually expelling them from the Zvornik municipality, these paramilitaries ..." Do you stand by that answer as to this sentence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was completed at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could now turn to 65 ter 17386, which is --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: It appears to be another document that you drafted regarding the Yellow Wasps operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any plans for the document which is on our screen?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I will tender, Your Honours, 65 ter 1D2255.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D2255 receives number P6581, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, have you been able to see enough of this document to determine whether this is one that you drafted?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: What is this document, just briefly?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a criminal report filed against Vojin Vuckovic and others who were all members of the paramilitary formation in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Just to make sure that I'm clear, is this the charging document charging the offences against the Yellow Wasps that you've described in your statement and your testimony?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there are also crimes that they were charged with. All of those things that they had committed in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Does the first part of this document, I believe the first two and a half pages, name those individuals who were charged with the offence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that there are several names there and then further down it says "and others," if I remember the document well. We could not name all of them, so we named only the most important ones and added "others."

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could just turn to page 2, briefly.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And let you take a look to see if that language is there.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, there is only one page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Perhaps I'll ask a question, and if you don't recall -- while we try to find the rest of the B/C/S translation of this document. If you don't recall, we'll come back to that question later. Following the list of people charged, did you then next go to the charge that these people were facing? Did you describe the offence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Is it correct that they were charged only with a violation of Article 151, aggravated robbery?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see the document, but if this is what you're claiming I am willing to agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: We'll come back to that question once we have the full B/C/S translation of the document. In the meantime we'll turn to 65 ter 9706, which appears to be another document that you authored regarding the Yellow Wasps operation as well. Have you been able to determine whether this is a document that you authored?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the purpose was for this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was our common practice before the war that once an operation was completed, it had to be analysed and then information was drafted. That information would contain all of the most important elements of the operation and then people would be informed, the heads of the Ministry of the Interior. And if that operation was significant, also the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina was also informed. And in this case, it was sent to all the relevant bodies in Republika Srpska. Due to the significance of the entire activity, we resorted to the old tested way when it came to informing the heads of the government and the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 2 in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'd like you to look at this page. And is it correct near the top of the page you detail the items which were recovered from the group including weapons, cars, and gold?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the second paragraph, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And then looking down to the bottom of the page, I have questions about a paragraph where it explains that persons will be detained pending charges and that others will be turned over to Serb armed forces or to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia depending on their citizenship. First, why were Bosnian Serbs being turned over to the Serb armed forces?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were military conscripts and there was a priority to recruit them to the military forces. That's why they were handed over to them. This means that they were not sent to serve a punishment. They were put at the disposal of the Army of Republika Srpska so that they could be referred to various units where they would then serve.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Can you tell us why Serbian citizens were deported rather than being prosecuted?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understand the criminal report well, those who were responsible for all those criminal activities - there were 11 of them - they were charged. And for the others who were members of the paramilitary formation were not charged and that's why they were deported; in other words, we could not obtain evidence to the effect that those people had indeed committed crimes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'd like to turn now to the last page in the last paragraph of your report, and I draw your attention to the information that Dusko Vuckovic, known as Repic, was committing massacre, genocide, over citizens of Muslim ethnicity. In this paragraph you explain that Serb armed forces, MPs, and national security operatives were taking care of this information. Did you follow-up on this information?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't do any follow-up. I was not in a position to do that because very soon after that I was removed from the MUP; i.e., I was chased away, to be more precise. So I was in no position to do any follow-up. But I know for a fact that this kind of information, either verbatim or somewhat different, was sent to the Ministry of the Republic of Serbia. I'm talking about Vuckovic and his brother Repic and the crimes that they had committed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Were you aware that Repic confessed to the military police regarding these killings in 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that detail, but I know that based on the results of our activities he was tried in Sabac and sentenced.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: We'll step through this in a focused manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- put one question in the meantime just to clarify. You said a minute ago, Mr. Andan, and I quote: "I'm talking about Vuckovic and his brother Repic ..." When I'm looking at the document, I see here "the information obtained by" some units "indicate that Dusan Vuckovic, also known as Repic" was committing massacre." It seems to be the same person, Vuckovic and Repic, or are these two different persons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were two Vuckovic brothers, Vojin and Dusan also known as Repic, if I'm not mistaken. Vojin was known as Zuco and his brother was known as Repic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. This clarifies it. And I have another question. On page 19, lines 20 to 22, you said: "If I understand the criminal report well, those who were responsible for all those criminal activities - there were 11 of them - they were charged." Can you tell us what you know about any prosecution, trial, sentencing of these 11 people? What happened to them after they were charged?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In legal terms, the Ministry of the Interior sends a criminal report to the prosecutor's office and that's where its responsibilities stop. That was up to the prosecutor's office. Neither as private persons nor officially did we ever want to do any follow-up. We were not allowed to do that. But in the meantime, I heard that they were never tried. There was a lady called Biljana, I don't know what her last name was but I know she was a prosecutor and she was the one who took over the case. I believe that she is still a prosecutor in the prosecutor's office of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. She is still a prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I understand from your answer that you heard in the meantime that they were never tried. What is the source of this information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard it from some private sources. I spoke to Davidovic, for example. I joined the army, we met somewhere. They were released. And around my house I saw Zuco observing, he was looking for me, and then I inquired about them, and then I heard that there were no charges against them and that they were all actually let go. They were released.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I still have a few questions for you in this context, Witness. On the basis of the document which is now on the screen, which is dated the 4th of August, you explained to us that the persons mentioned in there on page 2 in the English, Vojin Vuckovic, Dusan Vuckovic, Tanaskovic, et cetera, that they were to be sent back to the units --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tanaskovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That they were to be sent back to their units because there was insufficient evidence to prosecute them. Is that well understood? Perhaps we have a look at page 2 in English and most likely page 2 in B/C/S as well, but I'm not certain about that. Yes. You explained the line saying these person will be detained until criminal reports, et cetera, and then later it states: "Depending on the citizenship they will be turned over to the Serb armed forces or deported to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia." Now, you said: We did that because they had to be sent back to their units because there was no sufficient evidence to prosecute them. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, you didn't understand me properly. Perhaps I can explain, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 11 people who were handed over to the prosecutor's office did not not belong to the group of the others. In other words, these 11 were tried. The others were not because no evidence could be obtained to the effect that they had committed crimes. Those who were citizens of Serbia were deported and those who were from Republika Srpska were placed at the disposal of the Army of Republika Srpska. So we were talking about two groups: The first one that was tried and the other group which was never tried.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mean the other 54? We're talking about the other 54 that were sent back to their units.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And these ones, they were -- the 11, they were kept in detention for how long?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time, police detention could go on for 72 hours, I think; that is to say, without a prosecutor being involved, the police could remand people in custody for up to 72 hours. Once we would take statements from these persons and collect witness statements, when we'd complete the entire file, then the police detention would be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but you -- I think the charges were filed on the 28th of August, that is, 24 days after this report was filed. And it says: "These persons will be detained until the criminal reports are filed to the prosecutor's office in charge thereof in Bijeljina." But you say they could be kept in detention for three days, but you more or less announce here that you'll keep them in detention until the charges have been -- the criminal reports are filed to the prosecutor's office. When was that then done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The further procedure would be as follows: If the three days would be up, then we'd address the prosecutor's office and then we'd ask them to decide on detention. In the first stage it would be one month, and then if necessary it could go on. I as a legalist believe that if police detention would be up after 72 hours, then we would ask the prosecutor's office, and then they would respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was that done in this case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Probably, yes. If you have mentioned this. But then I don't believe that they could have been detained for a month. When all the documents are put together, that can be seen. But I claim if police detention was up after three days, then we would address the prosecutor's office and then they would continue their detention and that would be it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I'd like to know what happens rather than -- because on the 4th of August you write: "These persons will be detained until the criminal the reports are filed," I do understand that's for a couple of days, and I just want to know what happened after that. Were these reports filed, were they detained any further? If you know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the moment when we set up this file, then they were released, then it was the prosecutor's office that took them over, if you will, and they were the ones who released them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you transferred them to the prosecutor's office, and the prosecutor's office said: Let's release them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You know what the prosecutor did, but I told you about this part; that is to say, how far our powers went. Once they are handed over to the prosecutor's office, we have nothing to do with it any longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, and they were released. That's -- I'm not saying you released them, but the fact was that they were then released after a few days. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Obviously. Obviously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Bibles, I'm looking at the clock. It's time for a break anyhow. Could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes, Mr. Andan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break and will resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we are waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom, Ms. Bibles, according to our bookkeeping system, that is, Madam Registrar's bookkeeping system, you've got one hour and 15 minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I understand from Ms. Stewart that I might actually have a minute less than that, but I do anticipate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, well, then to be quite honest, one hour, 16 minutes was reported to me and not 1 hour, 14 minutes, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the truth is always in the middle. One hour, 15 minutes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, I promised you that we would go back to a document --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And that would be 65 ter 17386.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: -- once we believe that we had corrected the uploading issue with the B/C/S section. I'd like to do that now.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could go to page 3 of 17386.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, is it your recollection that we were discussing the charges that you had drafted for the Yellow Wasps? Is that your recollection?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: As you look at this page, does this help refresh your recollection or do we need to go to the next page?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's all right.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'm not sure that we have the right page in English up. Perhaps we could go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What you are looking for, Ms. Bibles?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: This document does not appear to like us today. Are we on page 3 in e-court on both pages? There we go. We're in the correct page on English. Page 5 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, does this page contain the charges which you drafted regarding the Yellow Wasps?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a description of the crimes that they had committed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And are we reading this correctly at the top of the page that they were charged with a violation of Article 151, which would be aggravated robbery?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see that article here. Maybe you can see it, but I see the description.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Three lines from the bottom in the first paragraph, just above "opis djela" [phoen]. You found it, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Are we correct that they were charged with violations of Article 151, aggravated robbery?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's evident.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And I'd next ask that we go to 65 ter 30779, which is a statement taken from Dusko Vuckovic from the 4th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, as this document is coming up on the screen, I believe you described that there were two Vuckovic brothers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Vojin and Dusan.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Do you see the name of one of the two brothers on the document that has come up on the screen?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Dusko.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Is he the one known as Repic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's him.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Could you take a moment to look at this document that's in front of you. And I would direct your attention to the bottom of the first page --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And I will turn the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Then we have to scroll down in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Have we indeed seen the last -- the bottom of the first page before it was turned to the second page?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Ah.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not fully.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Do you need to go back to the first page and read the bottom?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could we do the same in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I've seen it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could go back to the second page.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Is it correct that this is a statement in which Repic admits committing murders of non-Serbs at Celopek?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but on this page, Marko Pavlovic cannot be commander of the police station. He was head of the TO staff in Zvornik. Ratko was commander of the police station in Zvornik, whereas he here admits that he committed the crime of murdering the civilian population in Zvornik, non-Serb civilian population.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, I want to clarify the record. And first, to be fair to the record, Dusko Vuckovic was tried and convicted in Serbia after the war in 1996 of these offences. Is that your understanding?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think he was tried in Sabac and that he was sentenced to I don't know how many years in prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: But going back to August of 1992, is it true that he was released along with the rest of the Yellow Wasps who you had arrested?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think he was released. I think that we handed him over to the military police, as far as I can remember. And I think that that is contained in some documents, including this criminal report. Person number 9 was handed over to the military police.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Do you know who took the statement that we're looking at?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the operatives who worked at the security services centre in Bijeljina then. I don't know exactly. But a person from the crime prevention service, that's for sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this point I would tender documents 09706, 17386, and 30779.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 97006 receives number P6582, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You misspoke, I think. It should be document 9706.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, document is 09706. And it receives number P6582, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6582 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 17386 receives number P6583, Your Honours. And document 30779 receives number P6584, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6583 and P6584 are admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, is it your understanding that after the Yellow Wasps were released that they went to Pale and met with Mrs. Plavsic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had information that Zuco - and now, who was with him, I don't know - went to Pale after that, that he met with Mrs. Plavsic and Malko Koroman, the then chief of the police station in Pale. That's the information that we had. And I think that I spoke of that when I previously testified.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Andan, you've previously testified that as a result of this and other actions in the summer of 1992, that some Serb propaganda circulated at the time accusing you and others you worked with of protecting Muslims and arresting Serbs for small crimes. Do you stand by this testimony?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this specifically pertains to Bijeljina. The information service, civilians, radio television, local newspapers, they accused me and Mr. Davidovic of protecting Muslims and that we are arresting on false charges or trumped up charges "Serb fighters." As a matter of fact, at a session of the Assembly of Bijeljina, a request was made to expel me from the municipality of Bijeljina and to have him returned to the federal SUP.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And by "him" you mean Mr. Davidovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That Davidovic should be returned to the federal SUP where he had come from and that I should be expelled from the area of Bijeljina precisely because of what I told you about just now.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: In paragraph 7 of your statement and I believe at parts of your testimony, you have alluded to a suspension or being removed from the Serbian police. Is it true that following your work arresting the paramilitaries you were suspended from the Serbian police in August of 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said this. I never received an official document. I just told by Mr. Kovac, who had come from Pale to Bijeljina, he said that I should no longer come to the MUP, that they think that I shouldn't work any longer, and that they don't need me any longer. Just one more sentence, please. You will allow me. Let me say this: Mr. Kovac was very brazen when he said this. When I asked him for an explanation, he said this: Professionally you did everything for top marks, but we used you as a one-off condom. That's it. That was my conversation with Mr. Kovac and that's how I left the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: From the ministry you went to work with the VRS; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. A few days -- actually, I spent a few days in Bijeljina. I didn't do anything. Mr. Salapura showed up, I mean, he came to see me at home, and he said that if I was interested, if I wanted to, would I like to be transferred to the Army of Republika Srpska, and I accepted that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Is it correct that from September of 1992 to September of 1993, you worked as an intelligence officer for the 65th Motorised Protection Regiment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And I believe you refer to this in your statement that during the time in this assignment, you also led a sabotage detachment in 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Officially there was no commander of the sabotage detachment. For a certain period of time I led that detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Did you lead this detachment as part of Lukavac 93?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: In the statement provided for this case, you describe two times that you saw the accused with prisoners, both appear to be during Lukavac 1993; is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please clarify that question, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: In the statement that you provided for this case, which I think is in front of you if you'd like to review it, you describe two times that you saw --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's not on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It should be called up.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes. If we could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you intend to refer to a hard copy?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I was referring to a hard copy but it would not hurt to pull up this statement on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And I believe that's D512. And if we go to page 3, I believe, in both versions in e-court, which describes one of the contacts that the accused had with a prisoner. And then if we could turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: With respect to paragraph 16, that is the second reference that I'm alluding to here. Did both of these events occur during Lukavac 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, both.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Can you tell us if there were other times that you saw him with prisoners during the war?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 15 and then 16, the bulk of this portion of this statement, you describe this incident where you come upon of group of 20 to 30 Muslim prisoners. You noticed injuries on the prisoners. Were these clearly visible injuries?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was an incident. They surrendered to the Army of Republika Srpska in that operation that was carried out then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was whether the injuries were clearly visible. How they got there, who inflicted them is not the question. First, could you clearly see them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were visible injuries on the faces of some of the soldiers of the Muslim army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Is it true that you did not take statements from these prisoners, take photographs of their injuries, or interview the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because at that moment I was not in that role. I mean, that was done by the security organ of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: But you don't have information that those things were done by anyone, do you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: In fact, to the best of your knowledge, the order was that they be taken to Kula. Isn't that your understanding of where they were to go?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Mladic, who showed up there, he asked me: Who are these guys, where are they from? He said that the security organ should be informed, that they should come and collect them, and write down their names and that they should be transferred to the Kula prison, and that an adequate number of Serbs who are being held prisoner in Sarajevo should be exchanged for them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Well, let's go back to paragraphs 11 through 14.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Which I believe is the page in front of this or before this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: In these paragraphs you describe events surrounding a prisoner who is captured in Trnovo. Is this Asim Zulic that you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I remember his surname because as chief of police in Stari Grad, I had problems with the Zulic family. They were constantly involved in crime. And I remember that name very well. It doesn't have to do with this Mr. Zulic personally. It's some relatives of his.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Well, the next question I had is whether you knew Mr. Zulic prior to the war?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I had direct contact. Perhaps he knew me as a senior inspector, but I, as far as I know, did not know him. And I don't know whether he was an active-duty policeman before the war anyway.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your statement describes and what I think was captured in the summary is Mr. Zulic's attitude towards the accused and that that attitude was appreciative. I'd like to ask you some questions and some very specific questions about the evidence. In paragraph 12 you describe, with quotes, a statement that Mladic made to Zulic. Were you present when those statements were made?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was present.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Can you tell us where this conversation took place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where that conversation took place. It was in front of a house, in any case. There were several soldiers and officers there. Mr. Mladic turned up. He sat down with him and he told him, "Don't be afraid. Your life is guaranteed. You will be exchanged. You will be taken to the Kula prison." During that conversation, as far as I can remember, and I believe that my memory serves me well, he was offered a cup of coffee. He drank that coffee. And after that conversation, he sat down in a Puch car and he was transferred to Kula in that Puch, if my memory serves me right and I believe it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: At some point during that incident, did you become aware that Mr. Zulic was president of the Committee for Exchange of Prisoners?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way I understood it was that Mr. Zulic was an officer in the police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Who took Mr. Zulic away?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you. A vehicle came escorted by the police or the military and he was taken away. I don't know who did it, really.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Did you stay with General Mladic after Mr. Zulic was taken away?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I had some other tasks to carry out. I did what I had to do there and then I departed with the lads that I was with at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Do you have any information as to whether General Mladic spoke with Zulic a second time that same day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there only once.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Are you aware that Mr. Zulic was interviewed with General Mladic on SRNA the following day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never seen that. There was a combat going on, so I didn't have the time nor the opportunity to watch TV.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, I'd like to take a look at -- have you take a look at 65 ter 30758, which is a statement taken or given by Mr. Zulic in, I believe, 1996. If we could pull up the first page, to give you a reference.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. Despite having my spectacles on, I can't see a thing here.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: The B/C/S version is difficult to read. I'd ask you to --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Perhaps we could look more closely at the first paragraph in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, we'll turn to page 4 in both versions and focus on part of this statement. Do you see the name -- before we turn away there, did you see the name of Mr. Asim Zulic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're back on the first page where you may be able to read it. Could we zoom in on the first paragraph, especially the -- yes. Do you see the name of Asim Zulic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see Asim Zulic, son of somebody, born in 1952. I can see that. And I can see that the statement was provided on the 1st of March 1990-something. The year is not clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, I'd direct your attention going back to page 4. And then we'll turn to page 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And if we could go to page 5 in the English. And I'll ask that we focus on the B/C/S version near the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I believe as you look towards the lower third you can make the out the name Mladic, Ratko -- Komandant Ratko Mladic at eight lines from the bottom?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The last two words on the line 9 from the bottom, Witness. You found it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "At that moment the aggressor commander said Mladic," something, and then I can't read the rest. And he said: "Don't kill him." I can see that. "Report to the Red Cross, we'll see what we are going to do about him," is that what you had in mind? "In the basement escorted by the police officers," and then I can't see, "an unknown person or man, about 50 years of age, of medium height," somebody addressed him as president. And then he starts asking questions about Kolak and I can't see the rest of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, let's go -- really key in on the quote attributed to Mr. Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, could we have the bottom part of the previous page in English so that we see how it starts. Because that's the part apparently the witness read. Could we move to the next page in English. Please proceed, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, Mr. Zulic's quote, if you would look closely at this, as to what Mr. Mladic actually said, was: "Don't kill him and don't report him to the Red Cross. We will see what we will do with him." Wouldn't you agree that Mr. Zulic's recollection of the statement made to him by Mladic would be the most accurate description?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was there and I told you what he said. I can repeat that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Andan --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could move to page 5 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: -- Mr. Zulic describes that after his contact with Mladic, that he was taken into a basement and interrogated. He describes that although the interrogation was fairly short, that he was abused after he answered every question. Do you have any reason to doubt that he was interrogated after he was arrested?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no reason to doubt or not to doubt. I don't know who interrogated him. I don't know when.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, Mr. Zulic describes that he saw Mladic a second time that same day when Mladic came to the interrogation in the basement and asked him questions about troop strength and other questions about strategy. Wouldn't you agree that Mr. Zulic's recollection of that day would be better than your lack of knowledge with respect to those events?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in that position and I suppose that he remembers all the details. I told you what I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'd next like to turn to page 6 in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And I would ask you to look, even though it's difficult, at the top of the page in B/C/S for your name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see the name of Avdir Vatic [phoen]. I don't see my name anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, I believe seven lines down in the middle of the page you'll find your name, Dragan Andan. And in this page it's a little darker than some of the rest of the type, and that seems to be fairly clear. Could you take another look below the Avdo Vatric name?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with all due respect, a reference is made to line 7 on this page. I believe it would be fair to tell the witness that his name is mentioned on line 2 of this page because that would give the witness the entire context of the event, and it would only be fair. If the witness was aware of the entire context, he would be able to put Mr. Zulic's words into a context and only then would he be able to answer the Prosecutor's questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's very long for saying: Could we start at line 2 where the name is mentioned as well. Do we need to go back to the previous page or is it sufficiently clear? Because it seems that the name of the witness appears in the middle of a sentence. Perhaps we should ... Ms. Bibles, you will give the guidance.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes, if we could move back to page 5 at the very bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, I see you don't have your glasses on. Could you try to take a close look at the bottom of page 5 in the B/C/S version, please?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have my glasses, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps it's easier if you read it slowly to him, Ms. Bibles, because the quality of the B/C/S is not that good and difficult to immediately decipher.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Andan - and perhaps if we go to the next page, this will be of assistance - what the English versions describes is: "Dragan Andan, a former employee of the Serb" -- excuse me, "RS BH MUP, Ministry of Interior, came up to the car. He was wearing a uniform. He opened the door to the," and I believe it's "Puh vehicle," P-u-h, "and asked me, 'Do you recognise me?' I told him that I did and he asked where I was captured and inquired about the former Trnovo SJB commander, Avdo Vatric. I told him that Avdo Vatric had stayed with the army which left Trnovo. Dragan Andan closed the door of the Puh vehicle and we moved on." Do you have a recollection of that contact with Mr. Zulic the day after he was arrested?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, I believe you testified that you were unaware that there was an interview of Mr. Zulic with Mr. Mladic with SRNA?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: So would it surprise you to know that in an interview with SRNA, that Mladic humiliated and embarrassed Mr. Zulic during the course of that interview?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't comment because I did not see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Would it surprise you, then, if the behaviour of Mr. Mladic towards Mr. Zulic was so embarrassing that members of Mladic's own family tried to get him to stop?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why you are asking me that. I can only talk about what I personally saw.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, I'm asking you this because three paragraphs of your statement describe the incident with Mr. Zulic and describe that Mr. Zulic was appreciative towards Mr. Mladic. So wouldn't you agree, as a police officer, as a human being, that it would make sense to see what Mr. Zulic himself says about this incident?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but that's different from putting questions to the witness. There is a clear --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- view that this witness's recollection is -- differs from the recollection which we learned from a statement given by Mr. Zulic. But your last question was about a different matter, that is, whether this witness would be surprised that Mr. Mladic -- it certainly does not correspond with his observation of what he says he observed himself. And all the rest, Ms. Bibles, would he be surprised if his neighbours would have stopped him, if his family would have stopped him, if it happened at all, I mean, whether the witness would be surprised or not is not the most vital issue that we have to hear about. There clearly is a different recollection or at least a clearly different description of the event. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could see 65 ter 30759, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, an investigator with the Office of the Prosecutor spoke with Mr. Zulic on 13th of May, 2014, and you're now looking at or you will be looking at the statement that was taken. I would ask you to take a few moments - it's a relatively short statement - to review it, specifically with respect to the treatment of Ratko Mladic towards Mr. Zulic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And if we could go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: It appears you finished reading this page. You're ready for the next --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, your statement describes Mr. Zulic's attitude regarding his treatment at the hands of Ratko Mladic. You talk in your statement, and I believe it's paragraph 14, that even today Mr. Zulic is appreciative. Wouldn't you agree now that having read his original statement and the current statement, that his attitude about Mr. Mladic and the treatment he received is different than the interpretation that you provided?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Madam, Madam Prosecutor, my brothers Radenko and Mladen also surrendered to the BiH Army. They didn't survive. Their throats were slit in 1993 in Sarajevo. Zulic has stayed alive. We can have different opinions. We can have different views of various things. I told you what I saw. I told you what I witnessed. I cannot say anything about Zulic's statement after so many years for various reasons. If you want me to tell you what the reasons are, I am more than happy to share them with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, Mr. Mladic, you remain seated. You can consult at an inaudible volume. I hear you, Mr. Mladic. Mr. Mladic, stop. I can hear you even with my earphones on. So if you want to consult with counsel, you are able to do so but at a volume inaudible for anyone. The rule is quite simple. I am not obstructing that. Ms. Bibles, could you please resume. Or as a matter of fact, the witness has answered the question, I would say, yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, as I'm wrapping up here, thinking back to paragraph 6 of your statement, you advise that the Yellow Wasps were eliminated as part of the operation that was conducted and yet that didn't really tell us the whole truth about the Yellow Wasps, did it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In what context? What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: That the Yellow Wasps, in fact, were released after a period of time in custody, and they went to Pale and were received by Mrs. Plavsic and were not prosecuted for the offences. Wouldn't you agree that those things were left out of your statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already clarified that several times here. I told you that we filed a criminal report and it was up to the prosecutor why they didn't follow-up. As far as the police were concerned, the case was closed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, in paragraph 6 of your statement you say: "In that period there were quite a few police activities. Again, the struggle with paramilitary formations. And what is most important, the elimination of a paramilitary formation called the Yellow Wasps in Zvornik." Wouldn't you agree that that leaves out rather critical information and evidence regarding the Yellow Wasps?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, I'll move on. Isn't it true that in terms of value for the Trial Chamber of your statement, the most important aspects of your statement really isn't what you said but what you left out of the statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree with you. I answered all of your questions. I even told you what is not contained in the statement. So whatever may have been left out, I shared with you verbally. And let me just tell you that the Yellow Wasps as a paramilitary formation never recovered after our operation. They were never re-established as a formation and they were never active in the territory of the Republika Srpska after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender 30758 and 30759.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you remind me the --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: These were the statement of Mr. Zulic, the original statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the declaration?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And the declaration, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the declaration fits into what rule?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: 89(C), Your Honour. It's relevant. For one, he verifies the information in the first report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And a written statement taken for the purposes of this Tribunal where the witness does not appear for cross-examination, is that something that we would need to deal with under Rule 92 bis or 92 ter?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, we certainly could. However, given the testimony of this witness, both in his statement and in the courtroom, the argument would be that this is relevant for you to consider for the purposes of evaluating his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But Rules 92 bis and 92 ter are not talking about the kind of relevance. They give rather strict rules on admissibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I -- and I -- the first statement that was taken, the Bosnian statement, was not actually taken for the purposes of this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the reason --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- why I said this in relation to the second one and not in relation to the first one.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
